stories.headline: Trump signs memo letting vetted private firms run offensive cyber operations abroad

key_facts.fact: President Trump signed a National Security Presidential Memorandum on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, titled 'Expanding Capabilities to Combat Transnational Cyber-Enabled Crime', empowering US federal law enforcement to use cyber tools against transnational criminal organizations operating in foreign jurisdictions.
key_facts.excerpt: THWARTING CYBER CRIMES: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed a National Security Presidential Memorandum (NSPM) empowering U.S. Federal law enforcement to use cyber tools to disrupt transnational criminal organizations (TCOs) that operate in foreign jurisdictions to attack Americans.

key_facts.fact: The memo directs the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center to create a program authorizing 'Participating Companies' to conduct Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations against foreign cyber-enabled criminal organizations, overseen by two Executive Directors, one from the Justice Department and one from DHS.
key_facts.excerpt: The NSPM directs the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center (NCC) to create a program to conduct specific cyber operations that disrupt foreign TCOs, with two Executive Directors from the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security.

key_facts.fact: 'Cyber effects' operations are defined in the memo as including the manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation or destruction of information systems, networks and infrastructure controlled by information systems.
key_facts.excerpt: "Cyber effects includes the potential manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation, or destruction of information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon," according to the memo.

key_facts.fact: Participating companies must sign contracts with the DOJ or DHS, undergo 'rigorous vetting', and maintain a bond or escrow of at least US$1 million, forfeited on non-compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: Participating companies will have to maintain a bond or escrow of at least US$1 million, according to the memo.

key_facts.fact: The memo gives the program's Executive Directors 60 days to establish consensus operating procedures, and no operation may be approved until they are in place; each cyber operations package requires written sign-off from both the DOJ and DHS leads.
key_facts.excerpt: Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Program Executive Directors shall, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, establish consensus operating procedures for the Program that ensure the Federal Government's complete oversight and control of Participating Companies' performance.

key_facts.fact: The White House justified the move by citing more than $20.8 billion lost by Americans to cyber-enabled crime in 2025, and the memo builds on Executive Order 14390 signed on March 6, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Americans lost more than $20.8 billion to cyber-enabled crime in 2025... The NSPM is the operational follow-through on Executive Order 14390, which Trump signed on March 6, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Veracode co-founder Chris Wysopal called the memo 'a pretty big shift in US cyber policy', while the memo stops short of full 'hack back' proposals that would have amended the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.
key_facts.excerpt: Cyber pioneer Chris Wysopal, now co-founder of Veracode, called it "a pretty big shift in US cyber policy" that nonetheless stopped short of going as far as other "hack back" proposals.

stories.headline: Iraq and US set Sept. 30 as 'fixed and final' date to end a 23-year US military presence

key_facts.fact: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper in Baghdad on Wednesday, August 12, and afterward affirmed Sept. 30 as the 'fixed and final date' for ending the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS military mission and completing the departure of its forces.
key_facts.excerpt: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with Adm. Brad Cooper, who leads the U.S. Central Command, on Wednesday. Al-Zaidi said in a statement afterward that he had affirmed Sept. 30 as the "fixed and final date for ending the military mission of the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS in Iraq and completing the departure of its forces."

key_facts.fact: The pullout marks the end of a US presence that started with the 2003 invasion against Saddam Hussein; a US official confirmed Washington expects to complete the withdrawal by Sept. 30 but declined to say how many troops remain or where they would be redeployed.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military is on track to pull all of its forces out of Iraq by the end of September, officials said Wednesday, marking the end of a presence that started with the 2003 invasion against Saddam Hussein... A U.S. official confirmed that the U.S. expects to complete its pullout by Sept. 30, but declined to say how many troops remain in Iraq or where they would be redeployed.

key_facts.fact: Al-Zaidi said that from October 1 Iraq will be 'free from any foreign military presence and no weapons outside the control of the state', with militia groups also required to disarm by September 30.
key_facts.excerpt: From October 1, all foreign military presence in Iraq will end, with militia groups also required to disarm by September 30... Iraq will be "free from any foreign military presence and no weapons outside the control of the state" from October 1, Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi said.

key_facts.fact: Baghdad and Washington said relations will now shift toward economic, developmental and security cooperation based on mutual respect for sovereignty rather than foreign combat forces.
key_facts.excerpt: Iraqi media reported that Mr Al Zaidi had met Centcom chief Admiral Brad Cooper, and the two stressed that Iraq and the US will now move towards co-operation in economic, developmental and security fields.

key_facts.fact: The Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS was formed in 2014; US troops pulled out of most Iraqi bases last year but kept a presence in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region, where American bases have come under regular attack since the US and Israel launched war on Iran on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Last year, the US troops pulled out of bases in most areas of Iraq. However, they maintained a presence in the semi-autonomous northern Kurdish region. The American bases in the West Asian nation have regularly come under attack since the US and Israel launched a war on Iran on February 28.

key_facts.fact: The Iraqi government has set the end of September as the deadline for armed factions to surrender their weapons or place their activities under state authority, saying they will have no justification to carry arms once foreign troops leave.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iraqi government has set the end of September as the deadline for armed factions to surrender their weapons or place their activities under state authority.

stories.headline: US producer prices flat in July and annual PPI slows to 4.7%, a second soft inflation print

key_facts.fact: The Producer Price Index for final demand was unchanged in July on a seasonally adjusted basis, after edging down 0.1% in June and rising 0.5% in May, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Thursday, August 13, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
key_facts.excerpt: The Producer Price Index for final demand was unchanged in July, seasonally adjusted, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Final demand prices edged down 0.1 percent in June and rose 0.5 percent in May.

key_facts.fact: On an unadjusted basis the final demand index rose 4.7% for the 12 months ended in July.
key_facts.excerpt: On an unadjusted basis, the index for final demand increased 4.7 percent for the 12 months ended in July.

key_facts.fact: Within the month, a 0.2% increase in final demand services and a 2.2% advance in final demand construction offset a 0.7% decrease in final demand goods.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, a 0.2-percent increase in the index for final demand services and a 2.2-percent advance in prices for final demand construction offset a 0.7-percent decrease in the index for final demand goods.

key_facts.fact: Annual producer inflation slowed sharply from 5.5% in June and undershot the 4.9% economists expected; markets had forecast a 0.2% monthly rise.
key_facts.excerpt: Annual producer inflation slows sharply to 4.7% from 5.5% in June, also undershooting forecasts... Markets had expected producer prices to increase by 0.2%.

key_facts.fact: Core PPI, which strips out volatile components, rose 0.2% month-on-month in July, down from a revised 0.4% in June and below the 0.3% consensus; annual core PPI slowed to 4.2% from 4.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: The core PPI, which excludes more volatile components, increased 0.2% MoM in July, down from a revised 0.4% in June and below the 0.3% market consensus. On a yearly basis, the core PPI slowed to 4.2% from 4.7%, matching expectations.

key_facts.fact: The reading reinforced the disinflationary signal from Wednesday's consumer price data, strengthening expectations that US inflation is moving in a direction favorable to near-term Federal Reserve policy holds.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination of softer consumer and producer price pressure could strengthen expectations that inflation in the US is moving in a direction more favorable to near-term monetary policy holds by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

stories.headline: Trump claims 'total control' of Hormuz; Iran says strait stays blocked as traffic nears 3-month low

key_facts.fact: In a Truth Social post on Wednesday, August 12, Trump wrote: 'The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!', repeating a claim he made to reporters the previous day.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump made the statement in a Truth Social post on Wednesday, reiterating a similar claim he made to reporters the day before... "The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!" Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority replied on X that 'claims and repeated posts by U.S. officials that the Strait of Hormuz is no longer blocked do not change the reality: the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said in a post on X, meanwhile, that "claims and repeated posts by U.S. officials that the Strait of Hormuz is no longer blocked do not change the reality: the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted."

key_facts.fact: Kpler data showed vessel transits at a five-day average of around 13 on Tuesday, near the lowest level since May 12 and roughly 90% below the pre-war daily average of 130 ships.
key_facts.excerpt: Vessel transits sat at a 5-day average of around 13 on Tuesday, nearly the lowest level since May 12, according to a CNBC analysis of data provided by the trade intelligence firm Kpler... Traffic is about 90% lower than the daily average of 130 ships that transited Hormuz before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Supreme National Security Council laid out demands for reopening the strait over the weekend, including an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief, American troop withdrawals and war reparations.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Supreme National Security Council laid out sweeping demands over the weekend for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including an end to the U.S. naval blockade, sanctions relief, American troop withdrawals and war reparations.

key_facts.fact: Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a top advisor to the commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, told PBS on Tuesday that 'victory is on our side' and that 'we have also seen how the American military is weaker than what we perceived'.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a top advisor to the commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, told PBS in an interview on Tuesday stateside that "victory is on our side" and that "we have also seen how the American military is weaker than what we perceived."

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures settled up 7 cents at $88.98 a barrel on Wednesday and US West Texas Intermediate rose 7 cents to $83.27, with prices supported after a senior Iranian source said there were no discussions to extend the ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures settled up 7 cents at $88.98 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 7 cents to $83.27... Prices rose after a senior Iranian source told Reuters there were no discussions between Iran and the U.S. to extend their ceasefire.

key_facts.fact: Analysts disputed US Energy Secretary Chris Wright's Tuesday claim that the seven-day average for oil leaving the strait was up to almost 9 million barrels per day; Obsidian Risk Advisors' Brett Erickson said there is 'zero evidence' for the figure.
key_facts.excerpt: In a post on X, Brett Erickson, an analyst at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said there is "zero evidence that 9Mbpd is exiting the Strait of Hormuz per day". "Zero. Not 'maybe', not 'potentially'," he added.

stories.headline: Thoma Bravo to take insurance marketplace Accelerant private at $20.25 a share, a 49% premium

key_facts.fact: Accelerant (NYSE: ARX), a data-driven risk exchange for the specialty insurance market, announced on August 13, 2026 a definitive agreement to be acquired by Thoma Bravo in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: ATLANTA, August 13, 2026 — Accelerant (NYSE: ARX), the data-driven risk exchange platform transforming the specialty insurance marketplace through the Accelerant Risk Exchange, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement with Thoma Bravo to become a privately held company in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of more than $4 billion.

key_facts.fact: Class A and Class B stockholders will receive $20.25 per share in cash, a 49% premium to Accelerant's closing share price on August 12, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the agreement, Accelerant Class A and Class B stockholders will receive $20.25 per share in cash, representing a 49% premium to Accelerant's closing share price on August 12, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Entities affiliated with Altamont Capital Partners, holding about 82% of outstanding voting rights, have agreed to vote in favor; the deal is not subject to a financing condition and is expected to close in the first half of 2027, after which the shares will be delisted from the NYSE.
key_facts.excerpt: Entities affiliated with Altamont Capital Partners holding shares representing approximately 82% of the Company's outstanding voting rights have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the transaction. The transaction is not subject to any financing condition as Thoma Bravo has provided an equity commitment to fund the purchase.

key_facts.fact: If closing is delayed by pending insurance regulatory approvals, shareholders receive a ticking fee accruing at 6% per year for a specified period.
key_facts.excerpt: Under certain circumstances, if the closing of the transaction is delayed by certain pending insurance regulatory approvals, shareholders will receive a ticking fee accruing at a rate of 6% per annum for a period specified in the agreement.

key_facts.fact: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Accelerant reported total revenues of $356.9 million, net income of $80.0 million and Exchange Written Premium of $1.32 billion, up 23%, with trailing-twelve-month premiums of $4.6 billion; the company cancelled its earnings call and withdrew 2026 guidance because of the pending deal.
key_facts.excerpt: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Accelerant reported total revenues of $356.9 million and net income of $80.0 million. Exchange Written Premium reached $1,322.3 million, with a 23% growth rate and trailing twelve months premiums of $4.6 billion... The company cancelled its earnings call and is not providing 2026 guidance due to the pending transaction.

key_facts.fact: Accelerant and its backers raised $723.69 million in a US IPO in July 2025, a year before agreeing to go private.
key_facts.excerpt: Accelerant and some of its existing shareholders raised $723.69 million in an initial public offering (IPO) in the U.S., the specialty insurance marketplace said on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Zipalertinib hits Phase 3 endpoint early in first-line EGFR exon 20 lung cancer

key_facts.fact: Taiho Oncology, Taiho Pharmaceutical and Cullinan Therapeutics (Nasdaq: CGEM) announced on August 12, 2026 that the global Phase 3 REZILIENT3 trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival at a planned interim analysis.
key_facts.excerpt: PRINCETON, N.J. & TOKYO & CAMBRIDGE, Mass., August 12, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Taiho Oncology, Inc., Taiho Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and Cullinan Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CGEM) today announced that the REZILIENT3 trial... met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) at a planned interim analysis.

key_facts.fact: The trial tested zipalertinib plus platinum-based chemotherapy against chemotherapy alone as first-line treatment in previously untreated, locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, enrolling 285 adults.
key_facts.excerpt: This multicenter, randomized, controlled, open-label global trial enrolled 285 adults with previously untreated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations.

key_facts.fact: The zipalertinib arm showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement with manageable safety, and the Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended unblinding the study.
key_facts.excerpt: In this analysis, the study demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS in the zipalertinib containing arm. Observed safety for the zipalertinib containing arm was manageable. Based on these data, the Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended unblinding the study.

key_facts.fact: The companies plan to pursue US regulatory approval for the combination in the first-line setting pending discussions with the FDA, with full results to be presented at an upcoming international medical conference.
key_facts.excerpt: Based on these results, pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Taiho Oncology, Taiho Pharmaceutical and Cullinan Therapeutics plan to pursue U.S. regulatory approval for this combination regimen in the first-line setting.

key_facts.fact: Zipalertinib (CLN-081/TAS6417) is an oral, next-generation irreversible EGFR inhibitor and remains investigational, not approved by any health authority; up to 4% of non-small cell lung cancer cases globally carry EGFR exon 20 insertions.
key_facts.excerpt: Zipalertinib is designed as a next generation, irreversible EGFR inhibitor for the treatment of a genetically defined subset of patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Zipalertinib is investigational and has not been approved by any health authority... NSCLC is a common form of lung cancer and up to 4% of all cases globally have EGFR ex20ins.

key_facts.fact: Cullinan chief medical officer Jeffrey Jones said meeting the primary endpoint early at a planned interim analysis 'marks an important milestone for the REZILIENT3 study'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Meeting the primary endpoint early at a planned interim analysis marks an important milestone for the REZILIENT3 study and supports the potential role of zipalertinib in the first-line treatment setting," said Jeffrey Jones, MD, MBA, Chief Medical Officer, Cullinan Therapeutics.

stories.headline: FDA grants priority review to first potential Stargardt disease drug, decision due Feb. 2027

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted priority review to Belite Bio's new drug application for tinlarebant as a treatment for Stargardt disease type 1, according to a company press release reported on August 12, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA granted priority review designation to a new drug application for tinlarebant, a potential treatment for Stargardt disease type 1, according to a press release from Belite Bio.

key_facts.fact: The agency assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target date of February 12, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA assigned tinlarebant a Prescription Drug User Fee Act date of Feb. 12, 2027.

key_facts.fact: If approved, the oral therapy would be the first FDA-approved treatment for Stargardt disease type 1, an inherited retinal disorder causing progressive and irreversible vision loss.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA accepted Belite Bio's New Drug Application for tinlarebant (LBS-008) and granted Priority Review for the treatment of Stargardt Disease Type 1 (STGD1), a rare inherited retinal disorder associated with progressive and irreversible vision loss... If approved, tinlarebant would become the first FDA-approved treatment for STGD1.

key_facts.fact: The filing rests on the Phase 3 DRAGON trial, which showed a 35.7% reduction in the growth rate of atrophic retinal lesions versus placebo, measured by definitely decreased autofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence imaging.
key_facts.excerpt: The regulatory filing is based on results from the Phase 3 DRAGON trial (NCT05244304)... The company reported a 35.7% reduction versus placebo, measured by definitely decreased autofluorescence (DDAF) using fundus autofluorescence imaging.

key_facts.fact: Tinlarebant is an oral therapy designed to reduce the accumulation of vitamin A-based toxins that contribute to the progression of retinal diseases.
key_facts.excerpt: The oral therapy, which is designed to reduce the accumulation of vitamin A-based toxins that contribute to the progression of retinal diseases, was assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act date of Feb. 12, 2027.
